page.layout: One printed page of running text in a single column. No marginal notes. A strip of the neighbouring page shows at the right edge, and marks at the lower left are doubtful (see notes).

main_text.p: diebatur, manibus, calcibus, dentibus, unguibus, denique se mutuò impeten-tes, nec ab eruendis oculis, si possent, sibi temperantes: mox densati quoque totis agminibus in se ferebantur, mutuoque in euripum præcipites se agere summis viribus nitebantur: pugnabant pertinacissimè: cedere & victos se fateri habebatur turpissimum, potiusque ad mortem decertantes perdurabant, quàm ut hoc dedecus in se reciperent. Quod suo quoque sæculo in usu manfuisse[?] Cicero his verbis testatur. Adole-scentium greges ( inquit libro v Tuscul. quaestionum) Lacedæmone vidimus ipsi incredibili contentione certantes pugnis, calcibus, unguibus, morsu denique, ut examinarentur prius quam se victos fa-terentur. Quæ verba, quemadmodum & ea, quibus Paufanias totam hanc rem exponit, significare videntur, nudos adolescentes, ac sine armis certa-minis hoc genere defunctos esse, quam-vis Lucianus ὁπλομαχικῶν[?] nomine eos afficiat, vocabulo latius accepto abutens. Inter gymnica enim certami-na hoc etiam ephebo-rum exercitium referri communiter solet. Et quid pugnis, calcibus, dentibus, unguibus opus, si armis instructi dimicarunt? page.notes: Running head and page number are printed at top left and top of the text block, as printed. Doubtful readings: "manfuisse" at the line end (the printed word after "man-" is hard to read and is marked [?]); the Greek word after "ὁπλομαχ" is only partly legible and is marked [?]. Long s is rendered as s throughout, and u/v and i/j are normalised. Lower-left of the scan shows faint marks ("fi", "H", "ii"). These look like bleed-through or a digitiser's marks rather than a printed signature, so they are not transcribed. The right edge shows the neighbouring page's edge, which is not transcribed.
